comments.author: dist1ll
comments.story_title: Tales of the M1 GPU
comments.why_zh: 批评非整体式的操作系统设计以及众多隐藏的 RTOS。
comments.quote_zh: Timothy Roscoe 有一个很棒的 USENIX 演讲 [1]
comments.text_zh: Timothy Roscoe 有一个很棒的 USENIX 演讲 [1]，他是苏黎世联邦理工学院 Enzian 团队的一员。演讲讲的是现代操作系统设计中占主导地位的那种非整体式方法，这体现在大量独立、专有、文档不足的 RTOS 在单个系统上并行运行，最终导致操作系统研究乏味且缺乏亮点（例如 Linux 单一文化）。我猜硬件和软件行业的利益并没有很好地对齐，不幸的是这渗透到了操作系统的研发中。[1] [VIDEO]
comments.text: There's this great USENIX talk by Timothy Roscoe [1], which is part of the Enzian Team at ETH Zürich. It's about the dominant unholistic approach to modern operating system design, which is reflected in the vast number of independent, proprietary, under-documented RTOSes running in tandem on a single system, and eventually leading to uninspiring and lackluster OS research (e.g. Linux monoculture). I'm guessing that hardware and software industries just don't have well-aligned interests, which unfortunately leaks into OS R&D. [1] [VIDEO]

comments.author: jcgl
comments.story_title: C Isn't a Language
comments.why_zh: 现代硬件是处理器的混合体，而不是冯·诺依曼机器。
comments.quote_zh: 我发现这个演讲既引人入胜又有说服力
comments.text_zh: 这不是我该发表意见的领域，但我发现这个演讲既引人入胜又有说服力：[VIDEO] 简而言之，“计算机即冯·诺依曼意义上的机器”这一有用的虚构，并不能充分反映现代硬件的现实。不仅 CPU 本身不符合这个模型（比如推测执行、复杂的功耗与负载管理等），而且整个系统越来越是不同处理器和地址空间的混合体。
comments.text: This isn’t my space to opine on, but I found this talk both riveting and compelling: [VIDEO] In a nutshell, the useful fiction of computer-as-Von-Neumann-meaning doesn’t adequately reflect the reality of modern hardware. Not only does the CPU itself not fit that model (with things like speculative execution, sophisticated power and load management…), but the system as a whole is increasingly an amalgamation of different processors and address spaces.

comments.text_zh: 非常有意思。这让我强烈联想到 L4，以及它那种消息传递的风格。我很好奇它是否受到了 L4 的启发。这是一场很棒的演讲，唯一让我失望的是，我本来希望能听到后续会怎样。看完 Cantrill 引用的那场操作系统演讲 [0] 之后，我真的很想知道“一个横跨一堆异构芯片运行的操作系统长什么样？”这个问题的答案。Hubris 只是一个单节点操作系统，这一点有点让人失望，所以我会继续关注后续。 [0] [VIDEO] 补充：我去读了文档，上面写着：“最早提出这一点的操作系统是 L4，而 Hubris 的 IPC 机制正是直接受 L4 启发。”
comments.text: Very interesting. This reminds me a ton of L4, with its message passing style. I'm curious if it was inspired by L4. It's a great talk, and my only disappointment was that I was hoping to hear about what comes after. After watching the OS talk that Cantrill references [0], I really want to know the answer to "what does an OS that runs across a bunch of heterogeneous chips look like?" Having Hubris be just a single-node OS was a bit of a let down, so I will be staying tuned for the sequels. [0] [VIDEO] EDIT: Went to go read the docs and: "The operating system that originally made this point was L4, and Hubris’s IPC mechanism is directly inspired by L4’s"

comments.author: CrLf
comments.story_title: Disabling the Intel Management Engine
comments.why_zh: 主 OS 在更高权限的协处理器之下以沙盒方式运行。
comments.quote_zh: 关于这点有一场不错的演讲
comments.text_zh: IME 在这里招来很多恨意，但别被它分散注意力：更高权限的协处理器运行着主 OS 控制之外的代码，这正在成为（或者已经是）所有地方的常态。基于 Intel 的 PC 只是其中一个例子（也许甚至不是最过分的那个）。大多数硬件已经演化成实际上把主 OS 运行在一个沙盒之下，让它“以为”自己在掌控一切，但其实并没有。关于这点有一场不错的演讲：[VIDEO]
comments.text: The IME gets a lot of hate around here, but let's not get distracted by it: higher-privilege co-processors running code outside the main OS' control is becoming (or already is) the norm everywhere. Intel-based PCs are just one instance of it (and perhaps not even the most egregious one). Most hardware has evolved to effectively run the main OS under a sandbox where it "thinks" it is in control, but isn't. A nice talk on this: [VIDEO]

comments.author: jiveturkey
comments.story_title: Ask HN: Where can I find a primer on how computers boot?
comments.why_zh: 对现代启动过程的高层概览，以及操作系统之前的管理引擎。
comments.quote_zh: 观看大约从 10:00 到 20:00 的部分，可以得到一个不错的超高层级概览。
comments.text_zh: 这里已经有很多好链接了。我只补充一点：启动过程极其复杂，而且远早于目前这十几条评论提到的任何内容就开始了。我浏览了其中许多（不是全部），它们讲的几乎都是同一个故事，无论是在真实硬件上还是虚拟环境中。但现代真实硬件首先启动的是 Management Engine（或 BMC，或 T2，或类似的东西），它准备好一些事情并启动硬件控制器之类的子系统，然后才释放 CPU，让“OS”最终启动，而 OS 还浑然不觉自己运行在一个抽象层之上。观看 [VIDEO] 大约从 10:00 到 20:00 的部分，可以得到一个不错的超高层级概览。这两个也适合加深理解。[LINK] [LINK] 它们都涵盖了 UEFI，尽管重点是 T2。我知道这远远超出了你问的范围，但启动过程远不止 GRUB。
comments.text: Plenty of good links here already. I'll just add that booting is enormously complex, and starts well before any of the dozen comments so far. I skimmed many of them (not all) and they all tell pretty much the same story whether on real hardware or virtual. But modern real hardware first boots a Management Engine (or BMC, or T2, or similar), which prepares things and starts subsystems like hardware controllers, before releasing the CPU where the "OS" finally boots, blissfully unaware that it is running on an abstraction. Watch [VIDEO] from about 10:00 to about 20:00 for a decent super high level overview. These two are also good for a deeper understanding. [LINK] [LINK] They both cover UEFI, even though the focus is on T2. I know that's well beyond what you were asking for, but the boot process goes well beyond GRUB.

comments.author: RealityVoid
comments.story_title: Programmers Don't Read Books – But You Should (2008)
comments.why_zh: 现代 SoC 打破了简单的计算机模型。
comments.text_zh: 我想说，计算机架构可以有_很大_的差异，而且现代 SOC 里有一堆核心，它们在某种程度上打破了关于计算机如何工作的假设。我最近听了这个：[VIDEO] 缓存一致性、加速器、各种流水线方案、ISA 扩展。有很多很多东西一直在变。更不用说那些不断变化的软件胶水层了。我不知道 react 的历史，也不知道现代浏览器里发生了什么，但我怀疑存在操作系统约束、不断演进的 Web 标准、额外能力、不断演进的浏览器，它们塑造并迫使框架去适应。我怀疑人们只是为了变而变。
comments.text: I'd say the computer architecture can vary _greatly_ and there are a bunch of cores in modern SOC's that kind of break the assumption of how a computer works. I recently listened to this: [VIDEO] Cache coherence, accelerators, various takes on pipelining, ISA extensions. There are many many things that change all the time. Not even touching the SW glue stuff that changes. I don't know the history of react and what is going on in modern browsers, but I suspect there are OS constraints, evolving web standards, extra capabilities, evolving browsers that shape and force the framework to adapt. I am doubtful people change it just for the sake of it.

comments.author: hresvelgr
comments.story_title: Dear Open Source Developers
comments.quote_zh: 我最近在 HN 上看到了 Timothy Roscoe 关于操作系统开发的 Usenix 演讲[1]
comments.text_zh: 我觉得这基本上适用于所有软件开发者。软件及其系统在很大程度上是通过不断累积演化而来的，这会产生很强的网络效应，最终形成更高的应用栈。我们一直在把一切变得更复杂，因为直接用别人做好的东西就是更省事，尤其是当这些东西的准入门槛很低时，比如 Web/JS。稍微岔开一下，我最近在 HN 上看到了 Timothy Roscoe 关于操作系统开发的 Usenix 演讲[1]，我开始觉得，当旧操作系统架构的局限变得过于沉重时，现代计算可能会经历一次彻底重建，到那时也许就有机会“修正”应用栈，尝试更简单的方案。我真心希望未来的操作系统不要长得像 Linux，甚至不要试图兼容 POSIX。[1] [VIDEO]
comments.text: I feel like this generally applies to all software developers. Software and its systems have largely evolved through accretion and that creates a strong network effect and eventually, a taller application stack. We're continually making everything more complicated because it's just easier to use other people work, especially when the barrier to entry for that work is low, i.e: Web/JS. As a slight segue, I recently came across Timothy Roscoe's Usenix talk[1] on OS development on HN and I'm starting to think that a complete rebuild of modern computing might occur when the limits of the old OS architectures become too burdensome, at which point there could be an opportunity to "fix" the application stack and try something simpler. I sincerely hope the OS's of the future do not look like Linux or even attempt POSIX compliance. [1] [VIDEO]

comments.author: matheusmoreira
comments.story_title: I tested four NVMe SSDs from four vendors – half lose FLUSH’d data on power loss
comments.quote_zh: 操作系统其实并不掌管任何东西
comments.text_zh: > 也许我们可以把所有“智能”的东西都放到 OS 和应用代码里，然后只给我们的计算机接上商品化的 dumb flash 芯片。是啊，本来就该这么做，而事实并不是这样，这是个巨大的问题。硬件厂商隔离我们的操作系统的方式，和操作系统隔离我们的进程的方式一模一样。操作系统其实并不掌管任何东西，硬件只是给了它一台虚幻的、沙盒化的机器让它玩，而这台机器甚至都不反映硬件真正的样子。真正的计算机全都被隐藏起来，并由专有固件编程。[VIDEO]
comments.text: > Maybe we could do all the "smart" stuff in the OS and application code, and just attach commodity dumb flash chips to our computer. Yeah, this is how things are supposed to be done and the fact it's not happening is a huge problem. Hardware makers isolate our operating systems in the exact same way operating systems isolate our processes. The operating system is not really in charge of anything, the hardware just gives it an illusory sanboxed machine to play around in, a machine that doesn't even reflect what hardware truly looks like. The real computers are all hidden and programmed by proprietery firmware. [VIDEO]

comments.author: pietrushnic
comments.story_title: PC Engines EOL
comments.text_zh: 我不是 RISC-V 专家，主要依赖开源固件社区的知识以及 Ron Minnich 这类人物的观点，但据我所知，生产环境中 RISC-V 部署的大多数固件都是闭源的，所以我们无法判断厂商是使用 OpenSBI 实现，还是使用某种修改版本来达到他们的恶意目的。如果我需要被纠正，请给我指出那些明确说明自己如何透明地使用 SBI 的产品。有证据表明 coreboot 中存在对 SMM 的透明使用。SBI 不是 RISC-V 唯一的 TEE。还有其他概念，比如 MultiZone [1] 和基于 PMP 的 Keystone [2]，它们被宣传为可信执行环境。规范的开放在这里只有一点重要性——关于管理模式的 UEFI 规范也是开放的。但 IBV 们多次坑了我们 [3]，他们实现低质量的 SMI，可能提升权限，而规范并不保证实现者遵守它。缺乏工具使合规变得困难——随着各种初创公司将其视为机会，这种情况正在慢慢改变（例如 Binarly、Eclypsium？）。我的观点是，SMM 作为 TEE 并不是 x86 独有的特性，其他重要架构也有类似机制。OS 有办法判断自己曾处于 SMI 中，所以它并非完全隐藏，但仍然拥有超级能力。在 CNC 领域，SMI 延迟是从 OS 侧测量的 [4]。可信执行环境是把锤子，既可以以透明的方式用于好的目的，也可以用于恶意目的。进一步通常取决于可信……
comments.text: I'm not a RISC-V expert, primarily relying on open-source firmware community knowledge and the opinion of such figures as Ron Minnich, but AFAIK, most firmware for production RISC-V deployments is closed-source, so we can't say if vendors use OpenSBI implementation or some modified version for their malicious purposes. If I need to be corrected, please point me to products that state how they transparently use SBI. There is evidence of transparent use of SMM in coreboot. SBI is not the only RISC-V TEE. There are also other concepts, like MultiZone [1] and PMP-based Keystone [2], advertised as trusted execution environments The openness of specification only matters a little here - UEFI specification about management mode is also open. But IBVs screwed us many times [3] by implementing low-quality SMIs that could elevate privileges, and the spec does not guarantee that implementers follow it. Lack of tooling makes compliance difficult - it slowly changes with various startups seeing that as an opportunity (e.g., Binarly, Eclypsium?). My point is that SMM as TEE is not a unique x86 feature, and other significant architectures have similar mechanisms. OS has a means of figuring out that it was in SMI, so it is not entirely hidden but still has superpowers. In the CNC world SMI latency is measured from OS [4]. comments.text_zh: Android 上的 Linux 不会在软件主体之间做多路复用或保护。它曾经短暂地这样做过，但那导致了大量漏洞。因为 Linux 对硬件的看法（一个漂亮的对称系统，同构核心运行单一操作系统，共享内存地址空间）与实际情况不同。因此，硬件被从 Linux 中抽象出去，只用来运行 Linux 程序。它没有被容器化。它被隔离在一个 enclave 中，在那里它能造成的损害最小。Android OS 本质上就是一团专有固件的泥巴，再加上 Linux 程序和 Dalvik JVM。更多内容：[VIDEO]
comments.text: Linux on Android doesn't multiplex or protect software principals from each other. It did for a brief time, but that led to massive vulnerablilities. Because Linux view of hardware (nice symmetric system with homogeneous cores running single OS with shared memory address space) was different from what was the actual state. For that reason hardware was abstracted away from Linux and it's only used to run Linux programs. It's not containerized. It's isolated to an enclave where damage it can do is minimal. Android OS is essentially a ball of propietary firmware mud. With Linux programs and Dalvik JVM. For more: [VIDEO]
